data.narrative:
Black Forest Labs, an AI & Software company at Series B stage, is evaluated against a peer universe comprising 1 public company (Palantir, ticker PLTR) and 8 private firms in the same sector and funding stage, including Scale AI, Physical Intelligence, and Field AI.

Stage-Progression analysis was not applicable. The reported last post-money valuation of $3.25B implied a step-up to $6.2B, which exceeds 20x the company's total raised capital of $300M—a sanity check threshold suggesting data unreliability. Peer-Median analysis proved applicable, drawing on three same-sector, same-stage comparables: Scale AI at $29.0B, Physical Intelligence at $5.6B, and Field AI at $2.0B. The median of this peer set is $5.6B, with a range spanning $2.0B to $29.0B.

The triangulation yields a valuation range of $4.8B to $6.4B, centered on $5.6B. The narrow methodological basis—only one applicable approach—constitutes the primary uncertainty. The wide dispersion within the peer set ($2.0B–$29.0B) reflects heterogeneity in capital intensity, deployment velocity, or revenue maturity within Series B AI companies. Further uncertainty stems from the limited private comp data relative to the scale and specificity of frontier-tech valuations. Absent revenue or customer concentration data, the range should be treated as indicative rather than precise.
